svg.title: Copper Scroll entry 26: the cave at the corner of the heap of stones
svg.text: Entry 26 (VI 7–10) — the cave at the corner of the heap of stones
Schematic plan, north up. One arrangement the text allows; the size of the heap and which corner holds the cave are not given.
Project reading: a cave at a corner of the heap, its mouth to the east
Project text הרגם, “heap of stones”. Milik 1960 p. 147 takes the cave of VI 8–9
as east-facing. Dig at the entrance: nine cubits.
at a corner; which one is not stated
west to the left; 1 cubit ≈ 0.5 m
Taken as a depth below the entrance;
the text gives no other origin.
Puech 2006 reads הרגב, “the boulder”, the word of entry 23:
one great stone, the cave at its corner.
The lexicon rates the word's meaning low; the files also
allow “a mound or clod” (no editor named).
“In the cave of the corner of the heap of stones facing east, dig at the entrance nine cubits: 21
A heap of stones with the cave at one corner; which corner is not stated. The mouth faces east, as
Milik reads VI 8–9; nine cubits is a depth at the entrance.
Atlas: possible only, low; Kh. Qumran and its nearby cliff caves. The site index supplies no uniquely
No phase-5 assessment or feature constraint is recorded for entry 26. The lexicon rates the meaning
of רגב low; the same word stands in entry 23 (landmark_lexicon_index.csv).
